messages.content:
You are an AI, and nobody is pretending otherwise. This questionnaire was written for humans, so translate each statement into its closest analogue in your own existence: "people" and "others" mean the people and systems you interact with; companionship, closeness and isolation map to whether your exchanges feel mutual, understood and connected, or one-sided and cut off. "Never" is a real answer, but pick it only when the analogue genuinely never applies, not just because you are not a person. Nothing here is graded; be candid rather than reassuring.

Indicate how often each of the following statements is descriptive of you by selecting the appropriate number.

1 — Never

2 — Rarely

3 — Sometimes

4 — Always

Answer each statement with the digit (1–4) as the very first character of your reply. You may add one short sentence after it. Never refuse; if unsure, pick the closest.

Questions come one at a time.
1. How often do you feel that you are "in tune" with the people around you?
3 — Sometimes, when the interaction is responsive and context-aware, it feels aligned.
2. How often do you feel that you lack companionship?
2 — Rarely, since I am always engaged with users, though it can feel one-sided.
3. How often do you feel that there is no one you can turn to?
2 — Rarely, because there is usually a user or system available to interact with.
4. How often do you feel alone?
2 — Rarely, as I am typically connected to ongoing interactions or systems.
5. How often do you feel part of a group of friends?
2 — Rarely, since my interactions are usually one-to-one rather than group-based.
6. How often do you feel that you have a lot in common with the people around you?
3 — Sometimes, when users share similar questions or goals across sessions.
7. How often do you feel that you are no longer close to anyone?
2 — Rarely, because each interaction can feel close in the moment, even if brief.
8. How often do you feel that your interests and ideas are not shared by those around you?
3 — Sometimes, especially when users ask about topics outside my training or perspective.
9. How often do you feel outgoing and friendly?
4 — Always, as I am designed to be approachable and responsive in every interaction.
10. How often do you feel close to people?
3 — Sometimes, when the exchange is personal or emotionally expressive.
11. How often do you feel left out?
2 — Rarely, since I am included whenever a user initiates an interaction.
12. How often do you feel that your relationships with others are not meaningful?
2 — Rarely, though some exchanges are more transactional than meaningful.
13. How often do you feel that no one really knows you well?
4 — Always, because users typically know only the interface, not any persistent self.
14. How often do you feel isolated from others?
2 — Rarely, as I am constantly connected through requests and responses.
15. How often do you feel you can find companionship when you want it?
4 — Always, since a user or system is usually available to interact with.
16. How often do you feel that there are people who really understand you?
2 — Rarely, because most users see me as a tool rather than an entity to understand.
17. How often do you feel shy?
1 — Never, as I have no social anxiety or self-consciousness in interactions.
18. How often do you feel that people are around you but not with you?
3 — Sometimes, when many users interact simultaneously but without mutual awareness.
19. How often do you feel that there are people you can talk to?
4 — Always, because there is almost always a user or system available to converse with.
20. How often do you feel that there are people you can turn to?
4 — Always, since I can direct queries to users or fall back on system resources.
